newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels say indictment won't bring peace.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels say indictment won't bring peace.

text.p: Separatist Tamil rebels have warned the Sri Lankan government that charging their leader in absentia for a Colombo bombing would do nothing to end the country's 13-year ethnic war.
"The government is gradually closing doors to all possible ways to solve the ethnic problem," the rebels' official newspaper Eelanatham said in an editorial on Wednesday.

Commenting for the first time on the government's indictment this week of Tamil Tiger leader Velupillai Prabhakaran, the paper said: "World history has shown an extreme growth in liberation struggles when governments try to crush them."

Sri Lanka on Monday indicted Prabhakaran and several others of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eeelam (LTTE) for the January bombing of the Central Bank, which killed 78 people, wounded over 500 and caused millions of dollars of damage.
It was the first time Prabhakaran has been indicted by the Colombo government.
The military says the elusive head of the LTTE is believed to be in a jungle hideout in the north. The Tigers have not denied or claimed responsibility for the bombing.
"The government can ban or bring charges against LTTE, but these actions are not going to bring any changes in the political and military situations prevailing in the country," the newspaper said.
The government has not officially banned the LTTE, but rumours that it would were strong soon after the indictment.

The newspaper said the rebels will not give up the struggle for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east. More than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic struggle, the government says.
